# Measurement of environmental services generated by architecture in urban areas

The project seeks to strengthen the technical and scientific capacities of the National University to measure ecosystem services generated by buildings and public spaces in urban areas, such as: temperature regulation, evapotranspiration, water management, water cycle reconstitution, reduction of air pollutants, and regulation of air quality. Colombian legislation, through Decree 3172, created tax incentives for mechanisms for environmental improvement and control, which must be measured for their respective certification and verification by environmental authorities. While buildings are capable of generating environmental services and implementing effective mechanisms for environmental improvement and control, this regulation has not been implemented because of the difficulty of measuring such positive impacts. By acquiring specialized ENVIMET software (from German origin), and surface temperature and air quality measurement equipment, the National University of Colombia can be the first research centre in the country with the capacity to measure ecosystem services in urban areas in such a way that progress can be made in urban regulations that encourage sustainable and eco-generative practices for healthier environments and more resilient cities
